title: Latest successful backup with a self join
description: Return exactly one row per database and exactly three columns: database_name, backup_id, finished_seq. Use the latest successful backup for each database; a database without a successful backup must remain with NULL backup_id and finished_seq. If finished_seq ties, the backup with the larger id is newer. Use JOINs without subqueries. Sort by database_name ASC.
starter_sql:
SELECT d.name AS database_name,
       b.id AS backup_id,
       b.finished_seq
FROM databases AS d
hints: First join successful backups as b.
With a second LEFT JOIN, attach any newer backup for the same database; keep rows where newer.id IS NULL.
solution_explanation: The anti self-join removes every backup that has a newer successful backup.
